hook: Westlake has no aggregation, residents default to CEI PTC 11.24 c (Oct 1 to Dec 31 2026).
takeaway: Westlake electric aggregation ended as of June 2026 billing. No successor. The city rejected a 10.11¢/kWh renewal. Last supplier was Dynegy at 8.38¢/kWh fixed (Feb 2025 to Jun 2026). Administrator was the City of Westlake (consultant Brenda Fargo). Residents default to the CEI residential Price to Compare, 11.24¢/kWh from Oct 1 to Dec 31 2026. No gas aggregation.

rejected_renewal.note: City rejected a 10.11 c/kWh renewal offer. Not a current rate.

sources.quote: The city has posted an official notice stating that the aggregation program ends in June and that any customer who does nothing will be automatically returned to The Illuminating Company, which serves as the supplier of last resort.
Dynegy had been supplying residents at a fixed price of 8.38¢/kWh through June.
City administrators told council they could not lock in a long-term fixed rate below 9.95 cents per kilowatt-hour and turned down a 10.11¢/kWh long-term offer.
city staff hosted an informational session on June 23 with Brenda Fargo, the city’s electric consultant.
for now, the program is on pause while staff keep tracking supplier pricing.
Residential Price to Compare $0.1124 per kWh for October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026.

In the Village of Swanton, residents voted to participate in an "OPT-OUT" government aggregation agreement for electricity. This means all residents are automatically enrolled, but each individual has the option to opt out if they prefer a different provider or plan.
Current Agreement: Supplier: Dynegy. Contract Term: May 2023 – May 2026. Rate: $0.0696 per kWh.
This is a formal letter that has been issued directly to Toledo Edison/FirstEnergy on behalf of the Village of Swanton.
Village Administrator Shannon Shulters initially emailed a representative from FirstEnergy (the parent company of Toledo Edison) on January 5 to say the ongoing outages were unacceptable.
Swanton is not on the AMP Ohio member list.
